subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose external plugin-to-plugin Gateway method calls, and if so should the permanent SDK shape be raw dispatch, an allowlisted request API, or a typed service/capability contract?
rationale: This changes the public Plugin SDK and the Gateway authorization boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the caller identity, method policy, or compatibility contract.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
options.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Keep trusted-only Gateway requests
options.body: Leave arbitrary external plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls unsupported and document route-scoped HTTP or purpose-built capability alternatives.

options.title: Expose raw Gateway dispatch
options.body: Add a generic method-string caller and accept the larger security and compatibility surface as an explicit product decision.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved methods or typed capabilities with caller attribution, explicit authorization, docs, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current route-scoped dispatch contract that any broader SDK surface would need to preserve or replace.
